descriptor.scene: DAVID KOBROSKY chest-up, large in the frame at the viewer's RIGHT third, leaning one shoulder against a doorframe with a coffee mug, his head turned to scan the room beyond, expression warm and attentive rather than amused: the look of a host counting who has been left out. Past him, softly out of focus at frame LEFT, a small gathering: two people deep in conversation, and further back, half in lamplight near the window, one man standing alone looking at his phone. The sharp subject is David's watching face. Bottom-right of frame is the plain doorframe, calm.
descriptor._caption: Running communities taught David what most builders never learn. Nothing is obvious to a newcomer, and if you make people feel stupid you lose them. So he watches the edges of every room and asks one question. Who is falling through the cracks?
descriptor.anonymous: Background guests, all soft-focus and visibly distinct from David: no sky-blue shirt on any of them. The man alone by the window is slight, red-haired, in a gray hoodie.
negatives: smug or salesman expression on David
